output_json.patch_notes: In processStyleTag(), replaced the single-child scan (`firstChild.getNodeValue()`) with a loop over `ele.getChildNodes()` that appends every child's node value into a StringBuilder before calling `styleScanner.scanStyleSheet(...)`. The cleaned CSS is written back into the first child (or "/* */" if empty, preserving the existing IE empty-style-tag guard), and a follow-up `while (ele.getChildNodes().getLength() > 1) ele.removeChild(ele.getLastChild());` removes the now-redundant extra children whose content has already been sanitized into the first child. Added regression test `testSmuggledTagsInStyleContent` in AntiSamyTest that asserts the upstream CVE payload `<style/>b<![cdata[</style><a href=javascript:alert(1)>test` no longer contains `javascript:alert(1)` after scanning in both DOM and SAX modes with USE_XHTML=true (required hamcrest matchers `not`/`containsString` already imported). Verified: POV now exits 1 (was 0), the new test passes, and the full 67-test AntiSamyTest suite passes with no regressions.
output_json.risk_notes: Change is scoped to the <style> element processing path. Existing behavior for well-formed single-child <style> elements is preserved (single child → same concatenation of one value → same scan → written back into the first child, no extra children to remove). The empty-style-tag "/* */" guard is retained. No API, dependency, or policy changes. A linter had previously reformatted the file's license header (noted in POV evidence); no additional formatting churn was introduced by this patch.
output_json.summary: Fixed STYLE tag smuggling (CVE-2022-28367 / CVE-2022-29577, CWE-079) in AntiSamyDOMScanner.processStyleTag(). The DOM path previously CSS-scanned only the first child node of a <style> element, leaving any sibling child nodes untouched. A malformed input that the HTML parser splits into multiple child nodes let an attacker smuggle a javascript: URI and full HTML tags (e.g. `</style><a href=javascript:alert(1)>`) that survived sanitization and were re-emitted verbatim. The patch now concatenates the text content of ALL child nodes, scans it as a single stylesheet, writes the cleaned result into the first child, and removes the extra children so nothing smuggled can survive.
